div.head: Rect 21.4
div.ab: [21.4] Feola syndon folcgerihtu: on sumre ðeode gebyreð winterfeorm, Easterfeorm, bendform for ripe, gytfeorm for yrðe, mæðmed, hreacmete, æt wudulade wæntreow, æt cornlade hreaccopp ⁊ fela ðinga, ðe ic getellan ne mæig.

In quibusdam locis datur firma natalis Domini et firma paschalis et firma precum ad congregandas segetes et gutfirma ad arandum et firma pratorum fenandorum, hreaceroppum (id est macholi summitas) et firma ad macholum faciendum, in terra nemorosa lignum plaustri, in terra uberi caput macholi, et alia plurima fuerint a pluribus,

Feola syndon folcgerihtu: on sumre ðeode gebyreð winterfeorm, Easterfeorm, bendform for ripe, gytfeorm for yrðe, mæðmed, hreacmete, æt wudulade wæntreow, æt cornlade hreaccopp and fela ðinga, ðe ic getellan ne mæig.

Vielerlei sind die Gerechtsame des Volks: in mancher Gegend gebührt Weihnachtskost, Osterkost, Kost bei Geheissfrohn zur Ernte, ‘Gussmahl’ [Trinkfest] fürs Pflügen, Mahtlohn, Heuschober-Essen, beim Holzverladen [von jedem] Wagen [1] Baum, beim Kornladen die Feimenkuppe und viele Dinge, die ich nicht aufzählen kann.

Many are the people's dues [the lord's provisions for the tenants doing labour-service]: in some districts are due a Christmas feast, an Easter feast, a feast at boon-work for the harvest, a ‘pouring-feast’ [drinking-feast] for ploughing, a mowing-reward, a rick-meal, at wood-carting a tree [from each] wagon, at corn-carting the top of the rick, and many things which I cannot recount.

The people’s rights are many: in some communities they are due a meal at Christmas, a meal at Easter, a feast at harvest, a feast for the plowing, a hayrick feast for the cutting of the grass, a log in return for the carting of wood, the topmost grain on the cart for the transportation of the crop, and many other things that I cannot list.
div.note: The Quadripartitus read ‘midwinterfeorm’ as in 9.1, probably better. ‘bendform’: the Quadripartitus read ‘benf[e?]orm’, after 4.1c (compare ‘andfeald’ VIII Atr 19 f.). The Quadripartitus translated ‘lāde’ (land) instead of ‘lade’ (carting), and avoids the first person (as 5.1). Liebermann compares Rect 9.1 and 5.4.

Neilson Custom. rents 30.—Man verstehe unter benfeorm nicht etwa mit Toller Suppl. ‘beanfeast’, auch nicht bendfeorm ‘[Garben]-Bindefest’ mit Leo, Schmid; das -d- hinter n ist unorganisch; s. o. Wb II 45 Sp. 3; Sievers Gram. § 198 Anm. Über cibum precariae s. Neilson Ramsey p. 46; Vinogradoff Vill. 174; Andrews 280. Vgl. o. 5, 2³. In Battle ‘the tenants at the close of the third precaria were solemniter depasti’; Scargill-Bird Custumal p. viii. xxxix

On the peasant's Christmas feast at the lord's see Neilson Custom. rents 30.—benfeorm should not be understood, say, as ‘beanfeast’ with Toller Suppl., nor as bendfeorm ‘[sheaf-]binding feast’ with Leo, Schmid; the -d- after n is inorganic; see above, Wb II 45 col. 3; Sievers Gram. § 198 note. On cibum precariae see Neilson Ramsey p. 46; Vinogradoff Vill. 174; Andrews 280. Cf. above 5, 2³. At Battle ‘the tenants at the close of the third precaria were solemniter depasti’; Scargill-Bird Custumal p. viii. xxxix
Nicht ‘Gnadenschmaus’ (Leo). Vgl. gytesæl ‘Freude beim (Getränk-)Ausgiessen, Bankettjubel’
Not ‘feast of grace’ (Leo). Cf. gytesæl ‘joy at the pouring out (of drink), banquet revelry’

Med heisst ‘Lohn’; aber mæðmete ‘Heumahtessen’ erklären Leo, Schmid vielleicht richtig laut der vier vorhergehenden Composita sowie des zunächst folgenden; so las (laut firma) vielleicht Q. Das Kompositum fehlt Wbb. Besonderes potagium tempore falcationis prati, oder nach bedmath kam vieler Orten vor; Vinogradoff 147. 175; Hale lxxxij; Ashley Econ. hist. 51; auch deutsche Fronarbeiter erhalten bei Wiesenmaht einen Schmaus; Heyne Nahrung 139

Med means ‘reward’; but Leo and Schmid explain it as mæðmete ‘hay-mowing meal’, perhaps rightly, in view of the four preceding compounds and the one immediately following; Q perhaps read so (judging by firma). The compound is missing from the dictionaries. A special potagium tempore falcationis prati, or after bedmath, occurred in many places; Vinogradoff 147. 175; Hale lxxxij; Ashley Econ. hist. 51; German labour-service tenants too receive a feast at the mowing of the meadows; Heyne Nahrung 139
